    self_contained: true

---
The PeMS example contains hourly traffic flow for 16 June 2026 in the Los
Angeles area. It has 24 time rows, 4,112 active source columns and 4,435 display
links. The initial map hour is 16:00.

## Map and data

The map supports pan, zoom, playback and hourly selection. A road popup
shows the route, direction, endpoint stations and link flow. The summary
reports available stations, available links, link coverage and mean link
flow. Station-point and road-casing layers are selectable. Opposite
directions have a pixel offset that varies with zoom.

The HTML embeds the flow data, offline OSM geometry and Leaflet 1.9.4.
The documentation panel contains the preparation method, field definitions,
reference figure and statistics. The figure and selected-frame table below
use 16:00; the map readouts follow the selected hour.

## Source and data preparation

The traffic provenance identifies
`la_area_freeway_volume_2020_01_to_2026_06.html` and the June flow array
`flow_2026_06.binz`. The array uses gzip-compressed, little-endian unsigned
16-bit integers. Snapshot preparation extracts zero-based monthly rows 360
through 383 for 16 June, together with link geometry and column-to-station
mappings, into `data/pems-flow.json.gz`.

```{r preparation, eval=FALSE}
source('pems-flow.R')
prepare_pems_flow(
  html_file='la_area_freeway_volume_2020_01_to_2026_06.html',
  flow_file='flow_2026_06.binz',
  file='data/pems-flow.json.gz')
```

`prepare_pems_flow()` records the source files' checksums and the daily row
slice. The source rows contain hourly station totals formed from available
five-minute TotalFlow observations. Snapshot preparation selects those
hourly rows; station and link means are calculated during display.

The HTML build reads the packaged flow snapshot and `data/pems-osm.json.gz`.
`map-template.html` defines the map interface and includes Leaflet's script,
styles and license. `run.R` renders this R Markdown document in a temporary
directory and embeds it with both datasets in `largest-traffic-maps.html`.

## Fields and coverage

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source('pems-flow.R')
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path=file.path(tempdir(),'pems-flow-figure-'),message=FALSE)
```

```{r data}
snapshot <- read_pems_flow(params$snapshot)
osm <- read_pems_osm(params$basemap)
frame <- pems_flow_frame(snapshot, time_index=params$time_index)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item=c('Date','Hourly frames','Fixed stations','Fixed positions',
         'Active source columns','Display links','Selected daily frame','Timestamp'),
  value=c(snapshot$date,nrow(snapshot$flow),snapshot$stationCount,
          length(snapshot$positionStations),ncol(snapshot$flow),length(snapshot$links),
          frame$time_index,frame$timestamp)))
```

The network contains D07, D08 and D12 district links. It has 4,307 stations
and 5,065 fixed positions. The 4,112 active columns map into those positions;
a position's station ID links its observations to road endpoints.

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| `schema_version`, `source`, `provenance` | Wrapper format, `pems-flow` identifier, source files/checksums and daily slice. |
| `date`, `timeLabels`, `stepMinutes` | Date, 24 source-clock labels from 00:00 to 23:00 and 60-minute spacing. |
| `flowByHour` | Integer observations in active-source-column order. |
| `segmentPositions` | Zero-based fixed-position index for each active source column. |
| `positionStations` | Station ID for each fixed position. |
| `links` | Zero-based link ID, district, freeway, direction, endpoint station IDs/indices, absolute postmiles and latitude/longitude coordinates. |
| `initialTimeIndex`, `zoom`, `stationCount` | Zero-based initial hour 16, initial display zoom 9.4 and fixed station count 4,307. |
| `missingValue` | Missing sentinel 65535. Zero is valid flow. |

Available positions within a station are averaged. A link's value is the mean
of its available endpoint-station values. One available endpoint supplies the
link value; two missing endpoints produce a missing link. The calculation
keeps fractional means until display formatting.

## Hourly flow in geographic context

```{r map, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width='100%'}
pems_flow_plot(frame, osm)
```

Traffic links connect adjacent stations on the same freeway and direction.
Their geometry is separate from the basemap road geometry. The seven flow
classes have boundaries of 400, 700, 1,200, 2,100, 3,600 and 6,200 vehicles per
hour. A value equal to a boundary enters the higher class. Missing links are
gray; valid zero flow is green.

The interactive map scales widths and directional offsets in browser pixels.
The reference figure uses the initial zoom's offsets in Web Mercator. Daily
R index 17 and JavaScript index 16 identify 16:00. The corresponding row in
the June source array is R index 377 or zero-based index 376.

## Selected-frame statistics

```{r selected-summary}
values <- frame$links$volume
available <- values[is.finite(values)]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  statistic=c('Available links','Missing links','Minimum flow','Median flow',
              'Mean flow','95th percentile flow','Maximum flow'),
  value=c(length(available),sum(!is.finite(values)),min(available),
          median(available),mean(available),unname(quantile(available,.95)),
          max(available))))
```

The table summarizes available link endpoint means in vehicles per hour.
Missing links are excluded; valid zeros are included. The map rounds its
mean for the compact readout. Link values share station observations, so their
sum would not be an independent network traffic total.

## Daily coverage

```{r coverage}
stopifnot(nrow(snapshot$flow)==24L,
          identical(snapshot$timeLabels,paste('2026-06-16',sprintf('%02d:00',0:23))))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  position_hour_values=length(snapshot$flow),
  missing_sentinels=sum(snapshot$flow==snapshot$missingValue),
  valid_zeros=sum(snapshot$flow==0L),
  selected_links_with_values=sum(is.finite(frame$links$volume)),
  selected_links_without_values=sum(!is.finite(frame$links$volume))))
```

The day contains 98,688 position-hour values, including 101 valid zeros and no
missing sentinels. Coverage concerns the active source columns; some fixed
positions have no active column. The hourly construction sums available
five-minute observations without scaling an incomplete hour to twelve
intervals. Encoded values are capped at 65534. Contributing-interval counts
are absent from the snapshot, so a present hourly value does not establish
full raw-observation coverage.

The source clock labels are produced by UTC arithmetic. Their use here does
not establish the raw measurements' timezone or a daylight-saving conversion.

## Offline basemap

`data/pems-osm.json.gz` contains roads, water polygons and place labels from
the Protomaps OSM archive dated 20 October 2026. The extract uses zoom 9 and
the traffic extent plus a 0.03-degree margin. `download_osm.py` contains the
extraction procedure. Cache provenance includes the archive URL, retrieval
time, tile hashes, source metadata and a geometry checksum.

The geographic extract is generalized and split at tile boundaries. It
provides display context rather than routing connectivity. The basemap date
is 20 October 2026; the traffic date is 16 June 2026.

Map data: [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright),
via [Protomaps](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads), ODbL Produced Work.

## Build and figure export

`Rscript run.R` builds the HTML from this folder. R dependencies are `jsonlite`,
`rmarkdown` and `knitr`; HTML conversion uses Pandoc. Viewing the HTML requires
a current browser. Data preparation uses R package `digest`; basemap
preparation uses Python packages `requests`, `pmtiles` and
`mapbox-vector-tile`.

Daily R indices run from 1 to 24. Index 9 is 08:00. A figure-export call has
the following form:

```{r export-example, eval=FALSE}
pems_flow_figures(params$snapshot, time_index=9L,
                   output_dir='output/pems-20260616-0800')
```

`pems-flow.R` provides preparation, reading, link aggregation and PDF/PNG
export. Exports include link values, the selected frame as RDS and source
records. The HTML build and figure export use the packaged snapshot and
basemap cache.

## Interpretation

Flow measures the volume of vehicles recorded at stations. The displayed
links average endpoint values and are statistically dependent where stations
are shared. This flow snapshot contains neither vehicle trajectories nor
speed observations. It supports a spatial view of hourly volume; it does
not identify speed reductions or causal congestion origins.
